correctness.rationale: For pi<kappa<2pi the sampled matrix is unisolvent exactly when cos(kappa a) != cos(kappa); any singular sample-null cos(kappa x)-cos(kappa) has nonzero endpoint derivatives, excluding exact D. The central cardinal derivative D_11=kappa sin(kappa a)/(cos(kappa)-cos(kappa a)) and strictly positive P_11 force the exhaustive a=0, +/-pi/kappa alternatives. Explicit unique D, P are checked entrywise, trigonometric signs give cutoffs 4pi/3 and 5pi/3, and strictly decreasing mass residuals with opposite endpoint signs certify unique mass-calibration roots. The packaged standalone verifier passed 1,319 supplemental symbolic/high-precision comparisons. Finite tests are not used as proof of exhaustive classification.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary FSBP results establish general existence via positive quadrature and optimal-node schemes, but do not state the exact above-first-resonance three/two/zero geometry or its two uniquely mass-calibrated frequencies. In the stated band the derivative-of-products space is not Tchebyshev (its second-harmonic sine has five interior zeros), so the sufficient generalized optimal-node theorem does not directly apply. Targeted searches found no published equivalent within checked material; a specialized older formula remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete geometry classification for the smallest closed FSBP operator, motivated by the need for positive quadrature weights and well-defined energy norms in general-function-space discretization. Above the first resonance, two geometrically distinct aliased interior nodes remain viable when the midpoint loses positivity; the exact three/two/zero node phase diagram identifies intrinsic feasibility boundaries. Exact integration of constants is separately necessary in several applications; the two uniquely calibrated frequencies and exactly three grids quantify when that additional consistency is possible. It is more than reparameterizing a low-frequency result because the off-center cardinal zeros first enter the domain beyond pi. The result does not assert performance beyond this restricted algebraic setting.
